description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NHERI 2022: Post-Tornado Historic Masonry Building Reconstruction is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Rebecca Napolitano, Penn State University (psu.edu). Models of 12 historic masonry buildings damaged by an EF4 tornado were created by combining Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Structure-from-Motion (UAV-SfM) and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) point clouds. The building models can be used for different purposes, such as structural analysis. Additionally, the point cloud combination workflow can be applied to other projects. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-s0g7-ed50. Keywords: RAPID, masonry buildings, UAV, LiDAR, point cloud, tornado. Published 2022-08-19. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
